claim: GitHub issue #1290, which docs/operations.md cites as the technical detail behind its Active-Active approximate-prefix-routing warning, is a QPS/scale benchmarking issue and contains no statement that the precise prefix-cache index is partitioned across replicas or that Active-Active requires peer coordination/peer discovery.
stance_target: the idea that issue #1290 provides evidence that precise (not just approximate) prefix routing degrades in Active-Active EPP
scope_conditions: llm-d-router EPP, issue lifecycle May 24 2026 - Jul 21 2026
quoted_support: Understanding QPS and concurrency limits for EPP in active-active mode for: Various configurations: with/without precise prefix cache aware routing; Replication level, 2 vs 3 vs 4 on medium and large CPU machine types on cloud

claim: Empirical GPU benchmark data in issue #1290 shows precise-prefix-cache Active-Active EPP failure counts at 500 QPS DECREASE monotonically as replica count increases (1r broken/3,148 failures to 4r 18 failures), with TTFT P50 dropping from 165ms to 30ms.
stance_target: the draft's claim that precise prefix routing is safe/effective under Active-Active EPP
scope_conditions: real vLLM v0.19.1 serving Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on 3x1 GPU pods, standalone EPP mode
quoted_support: Precise prefix cache active-active scaling: 1 | 165ms | broken | 3,148; 2 | 59ms | 295ms | 57; 3 | 41ms | 139ms | 31; 4 | 30ms | 96ms | 18

claim: The llm-d-router standalone Helm chart auto-injects --ha-enable-leader-election whenever router.epp.replicas > 1, silently forcing active-passive behavior (1-replica throughput) unless operators explicitly set it to false.
stance_target: operational gotchas of deploying multi-replica EPP
quoted_support: Leader election trap. The standalone chart auto-enables --ha-enable-leader-election when replicas > 1. This makes it active-passive (only leader processes traffic). Deploying 4 replicas without disabling it gives 1-replica throughput.

claim: Session-affinity-filter correctness under Active-Active EPP replicas was never validated in issue #1290 -- testing used synthetic independent requests with no session-token echoing, and the issue explicitly defers cross-replica session-pinning validation to a separate, undone evaluation.
stance_target: whether session affinity state is safely handled across Active-Active EPP replicas
quoted_support: Session pinning latency benefit (KV cache reuse on repeat requests) requires trace replay with session header echoing, which is a separate evaluation.

claim: Audited absence: issue #1290 (and its linked commits/PRs) contains no mention of LRU/no-hit-lru scorer state or predicted-latency-scorer training state differing per replica in Active-Active mode; the only per-replica-divergent state documented anywhere in the vault's llm-d-router sources is flow-control/saturation-view state (from docs/operations.md, not from #1290).
stance_target: completeness of known per-replica state divergence risks in Active-Active EPP
scope_conditions: searched issue #1290 full text and linked commit/PR titles
quoted_support: Findings: 1. Leader election trap... 2. Cold-start penalty... 3. Scale replicas, not CPU.
